messages:
marcus: heads up — dashboards spiking, auth-failure rate ~1.2k/min across multiple orgs, looks like SSO gateway errors and a lot of fallback sign-ins. cc @alisha @kevin
sec-bot: ALERT 1809123456: auth.anomaly.rate_limit_exceeded detected (threshold 300/m). sample src_ips: 45.77.13.22, 18.204.1.5, 185.82.200.11
alisha: grabbing logs now. are these all failed SSO flows or mixed SSO+password?
kevin: initial query shows ~70% SSO failure then attempts to fallback to local auth. suspicious pattern -> MFA push fatigue + credential stuffing maybe.
marcus: here's a short grep from auth logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-20T18:12:14Z user=jane@acme.com method=SSO status=FAIL reason=invalid_assertion src=45.77.13.22
2026-03-20T18:12:18Z user=jane@acme.com method=LOCAL status=FAIL reason=bad_password src=45.77.13.22
2026-03-20T18:12:21Z user=jane@acme.com method=LOCAL status=SUCCESS src=18.204.1.5
2026-03-20T18:12:25Z user=tom@oscorp.com method=SSO status=SUCCESS src=52.86.23.11
2026-03-20T18:12:27Z user=tom@oscorp.com method=SSO status=SUCCESS src=5.188.12.7
```
kevin: note the identical users with near-simultaneous logins from different geo IPs -> impossible travel. could be IP spoofing via proxies.
olga: oncall here. I've throttled the SSO endpoint at the edge (nginx rate-limit per IP + per-user) and added temporary rule to reject IEC ranges we commonly see in abuse.
dana: thanks. can you post the exact commands you ran? need to include in incident log.
olga: ran this on edge:
```
sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 185.82.200.0/24 -j DROP
# nginx conf snippet added to rate limit by $binary_remote_addr and $arg_user
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=rl:10m rate=30r/m;
```
alisha: blocked the suspicious src_ips in the WAF and triggered session revoke for impacted users. using admin API:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/sessions/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"users": ["jane@acme.com","tom@oscorp.com"], "reason": "suspected account compromise"}'
```
marcus: can we disable SSO fallback to local auth for 30m? that's the likely vector for lateral access once SSO fails.
kevin: agreed — change is needed. I'll flip flag in config and deploy a quick patch to the auth service: set ALLOW_SSO_FALLBACK=false for the tenant-global policy. rolling out now.
sec-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: ALLOW_SSO_FALLBACK updated by kevin at 18:16Z; audit_event_id=audit_1809123501
alisha: MFA provider shows a huge push volume — looks like MFA fatigue attacks. we should notify affected orgs. drafting comms.
dana: Ops/Trust will want timeline + mitigation steps. I'll open a support-cases batch and include recommended actions: rotate SSO certs, enforce phishing-resistant MFA.
olga: observed a small number of successful local logins that we revoked. added user-level forced password reset for those accounts.
marcus: ok next steps — short list: 1) keep edge throttles for 24h 2) disable SSO fallback for 1h and monitor 3) force rotate SSO client secrets for tenants with >5 failed attempts 4) add SIEM rule for impossible-travel within 2m window
kevin: I'm pushing an emergency rule to the auth-service to emit explicit audit events for fallback attempts (new field: auth_attempt.fallback=true) and to tag suspicious IPs.
alisha: created incident in pagerduty and ticket INC-2026-198. writing initial postmortem stub.
dana: comms sent to affected customers: short notice + recommended actions + we offered targeted help.
olga: we should add a runbook item: if SSO failures + fallback attempts spike > 200/min, automatically disable fallback for affected tenant and escalate to sec-oncall.
marcus: agree. also file a task for KMS team to verify rotation ops — if we rotate client secrets, ensure they propagate to Dedicated/Private deployments. add owners.
kevin: quick check — are there any indications of credential exfil? logs show no unusual API keys requests, mostly auth endpoints.
alisha: no app-level keys used, seems confined to auth surface. still treat as high risk.
marcus: final ask: please attach snippets of sanitized logs and the WAF/nginx diffs to INC-2026-198. Also add timeline and who performed each action.
dana: will do. assigning follow-ups: olga -> edge rules and runbook; kevin -> auth-service audit events + disable fallback flag rollback plan; alisha -> customer comms + postmortem; marcus -> coordinate KMS/client secret rotation and PM note.
kevin: noted. restoring normal policies in 1h if no new anomalies.
marcus: thanks team. patching incident notes now. :thumbsup:
